summary: Tested the global 'Local recusado' filter (blocked_places). Backend: 23/23 new tests pass. They cover the default empty list (new docs, docs without the field, legacy single-app docs), trimming and collapsing spaces, removing case-insensitive duplicates, dropping empty entries, keeping other fields unchanged, clearing the list with [], 422 for an entry of 81 characters or more and for 201 items (80 characters and 200 items are accepted), 422 for a non-list value, and 401/403 without auth. A Python simulation of blockedPlace()/fold() passes: Jardim Petropolis matches 'Jardim Petrópolis', centro matches CENTRO, Centro does NOT match Centronorte, Parque matches Parque Industrial, Zona 7 does NOT match Zona 70, and accents are ignored. Regression: test_exclusive_finish_texts.py and test_reject_notify_master.py pass with -n0 (34/34 in total). Frontend at 375px: the Painel renders after CPF login. The section 'LOCAIS RECUSADOS · TODOS OS APPS' shows. Adding works with the + button and with Enter, the input is trimmed and cleared, and the same name in different case is not duplicated. Removing a chip works, and blocked-places-empty shows when the list is empty. The list stays the same when switching between RapidoCar and MooveCar. Salvar Filtros saves it (toast 'Filtros salvos', MongoDB checked) and it survives a reload. Chips wrap correctly and a long name is cut with an ellipsis inside the card. Kotlin static review found no compile errors.

ui_bugs.issue: There is no maxLength on blocked-place-input. A name longer than 80 characters is added as a chip, then Salvar Filtros fails with the generic toast 'Erro ao salvar. Tente novamente.' (the API returns 422). The user cannot tell which chip is the problem. Add maxLength={80} to the input (filtros.tsx:500).

issues: The chip remove icon is 18x20. With hitSlop 10 the touch area is about 38x40, a little under 44pt. Consider hitSlop 12 or more (filtros.tsx:523).

action_items: LOW: add maxLength={80} to blocked-place-input (filtros.tsx:500), so an entry that is too long cannot be saved and cause a generic error.
LOW: increase hitSlop on blocked-place-remove-* to reach a 44pt touch target.

OPTIONAL (Kotlin robustness, do not touch the accept/reading logic): fold() uses \s+, which does not match NBSP (U+00A0) on Android/Java without UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS. Use Regex("[\\s\\u00A0]+"), so 'Jardim\u00A0Petrópolis' still matches.

OPTIONAL: check with Modo aprendizado on a real device that the pickup and destination addresses appear in the text passed to blockedPlace ('$priceText | $kmText'). offerText() returns the smallest scope with 2 or more km, which may not include address nodes on some card layouts.
critical_code_review_comments: RideAccessibilityService.kt:25 imports java.text.Normalizer. Lines 412-425: blockedPlace/fold are correct Kotlin. JSONArray.optString(i, "") is valid, Regex.escape gives \Q..\E, and the boundary Regex '(^|[^\p{L}\p{N}])…($|[^\p{L}\p{N}])' is escaped correctly in the Kotlin string. Locale is imported. No compile errors found.

Line 236: the call site reasons.put("Local recusado: $it") runs after the price, minimum and pickup checks and before 'accepted'. So a blocked place leads to a refusal, and to auto-reject when reject_enabled is on. The accept and offer-reading logic is unchanged.
The matching text is '$priceText | $kmText'. Text nodes are joined with ' | ', so a place name split across two nodes will not match (an edge case).
The Regex is compiled for every place on every offer (up to 200). This is acceptable, but the patterns could be precompiled when the config changes.
Backend: the dedupe uses str.lower(), not casefold(), and does not ignore accents. 'Petropolis' and 'Petrópolis' are both kept. This is harmless, because the Kotlin matching ignores accents.
